title: Multidisciplinary examination of putrefaction fluid deposits \(PFD) for forensic and anthropological purposes
protocol: Sample at least a 1-cm-long fragment of PFD directly into the skull during an anthropological or archaeological survey.
Clean each sample by fine scraping with non-contaminating plastic instruments.
Vaporize pressured air on all faces of the sample for 10 minutes.
Perform environmental SEM examination using Philips XL30 CP with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.
Fine fragment the PFD sample to enhance fixative penetration and facilitate rehydration.
Immerse the fragmented PFD in 20% diluted acetic acid for 48 hours to decalcify slowly.
Sample 200 μl from the supernatant of PFD suspension.
Centrifuge the sample at 800 rpm for 10 min.
Produce two spots per slide from the centrifuged sample.
Fix the spots on four slides with lacquer or air drying.
Color two slides using the Papanicolaou technique after fixing.
Color the remaining two slides using the May–Grünwald–Giemsa (MGG) technique after fixing.
Centrifuge the remaining solid phase at 3,500 rpm for 10 minutes.
Keep the supernatant in reserve for possible cytological study.
Recuperate the base and fix it in AFA solution (acetic acid, formaldehyde, alcohol) for 24 hours.
After fixation and decalcification, place the sample in a cassette on foam.
Proceed with dehydration in xylene followed by increasing alcohol baths.
Include the sample in liquid paraffin and cool it down.
Section the sample using a microtome to obtain sections of 6 to 10 μm thickness.
Deposit the sections on an albumenized slide, then air-dry freely.
Dewax the slide and rehydrate it by immersion in xylene followed by decreasing alcohol baths to distilled water.
Stain each sample with periodic acid Schiff.
Stain each sample with Gram stain.
Stain each sample with toluidine blue.
Stain each sample with hematoxylin, eosin, saffron (HES).
